newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Steel outlook remains positive.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Steel outlook remains positive.

text.p: USX-U.S. Steel Group said Wednesday its outlook remains positive to extend first half gains into the second half 1997.

Boosted by a continued strong market and good operating and shipment performance, the company reported second quarter net income, adjusted for special items, was $110 million, or $1.26 per share, adding "This was a substantial improvement over second quarter 1996 net income, adjusted for special items, of $34 million, or $0.35 per share."
The First Call consensus for the latest quarter was $1.16 per share.
"We're seeing a continued healthy order book for sheet products and improvements in tubular markets," Chairman Thomas Usher said.

"With current market conditions and anticipated strong operating performance throughout U.S. Steel's facilities, we should be well-positioned to extend these strong first-half results into the second-half of 1997."

It is anticipated that in the third quarter U.S. Steel will conclude settlement with its insurers regarding claims related to the April 2, 1996, hearth break-out at the Gary No. 13 blast furnace, the company said.

Proceeds from the settlement are expected to be received and will increase operating income by $25 million in third quarter 1997. A partial settlement of $15 million additional was received in the first quarter of 1997.

U.S. Steel's 1997 provision for estimated income taxes has been increased, primarily due to a reduction in estimated tax credits for the year. The six month effect of this revised estimate was recorded in the second quarter, it said.
Second quarter revenues were $1.7 billion in 1997 and $1.6 billion in 1996.

The Steel Group said its operating income in second quarter 1997 was $177 million on shipments of 2.9 million tons. This compares with operating income in second quarter 1996 of $1 million on shipments of 2.7 million tons.
It said second quarter 1996 operating income included $59 million in pretax charges related to the No. 13 blast furnace repairs and unrelated legal accruals.

Commenting on the latest quarter, Usher said, "The company's strong financial performance reflected ongoing attention to customer needs, operating efficiencies and cost reductions throughout our facilities."
The Group's raw steel producing facilities operated at more than 99 percent of capability during the quarter, compared with an 80 percent operating rate in second quarter 1996, it said .
A planned reline outage at the No. 1 blast furnace at Mon Valley (Pa.) Works began in mid-June and is scheduled for completion in early September.
